settings.config.sessions.intro: These rules decide when an end user's session ends. They are checked on every request the user makes.
settings.config.sessions.lifetime.title: Session lifetime
settings.config.sessions.lifetime.intro: A session ends when it is unused for too long or reaches its maximum age.
settings.config.sessions.inactivity.hint: A session unused for this long becomes idle and ends as 'Timed out' on its next request or at the next idle check. Also decides who counts as online.
settings.config.sessions.maxAge.label: Maximum session age
settings.config.sessions.maxAge.hint: Counted from sign-in, regardless of activity. Applied on the session's next request; until then the session can still show as active or idle.
settings.config.sessions.lastSeen.label: Update "Last active" at most every
settings.config.sessions.lastSeen.hint: Lower values make 'Last active' and idle detection more precise but write to the database more often.
settings.config.sessions.lastSeen.warnin: This is not clearly shorter than the inactivity timeout, so sessions in use can show as idle.
settings.config.sessions.idleCheck.label: Run idle check every
settings.config.sessions.idleCheck.hint: The idle check ends idle sessions as 'Timed out'. It deletes nothing. It also runs once at server start.
settings.config.sessions.idleMethod.hint: Direct SQL is faster but skips lifecycle hooks. Ignored when Strapi's refresh-token mode is on.
settings.config.token.title: Token check
settings.config.token.intro: Decides what happens to a token that Session Manager has no record for. Ended, expired and revoked sessions and blocked users are always rejected.
settings.config.token.check.label: Strict token check
settings.config.token.check.hint: Rejects tokens without a session record and requests where the check itself fails.
settings.config.token.relaxedWarning: Tokens without a session record are accepted. If the check itself fails, up to 10 requests per minute are still allowed.
settings.config.token.grace.label: Grace period after sign-in
settings.config.token.grace.hint: Accepts a new token for a few seconds while its session record is being created. Only for tokens without a session record. Not used when Strapi's refresh-token mode (jwtManagement: 'refresh') is on.
settings.config.token.key.label: Token encryption key
settings.config.token.key.hint: Session Manager encrypts stored tokens with this environment variable. Not needed in Strapi's refresh-token mode. Nothing is saved here.
settings.config.token.key.placeholder: Select Generate key to create a key.
settings.config.token.key.copied: Copied. Add it to your server environment and restart Strapi.
settings.config.rejected.title: When a session is rejected
settings.config.rejected.intro: What your app receives when a request uses an ended session.
settings.config.rejected.body: The response is 401 with the header {header} and the reason: {reasons}.
settings.config.rejected.reason.manual: Ended from the Strapi admin, or by the user from another of their devices.
settings.config.rejected.reason.idle: Not used for longer than the inactivity timeout.
settings.config.rejected.reason.blocked: Ended because the user account was blocked.
settings.config.loginProtection.intro: These rules check new sign-ins before they succeed. Existing sessions are not affected. Failed and refused sign-ins are recorded in the security log while recording is on.
settings.config.failed.title: Failed sign-ins
settings.config.failed.intro: Slows down password guessing. Counts are shared by every server process.
settings.config.failed.lockout.label: Lock an IP address after
settings.config.failed.lockout.hint: A whole number from 0 to 100. 0 turns the IP lockout off.
settings.config.clientIp.title: Client IP address
settings.config.clientIp.intro: All IP-based rules depend on reading the real client address.
settings.config.clientIp.trustProxy.hint: Turn on only behind a proxy you control. Affects the recorded IP address, the IP lockout and location lookups.
settings.config.suspicious.title: Suspicious sign-ins
settings.config.suspicious.intro: Refuses new sign-ins that look risky.
settings.config.suspicious.reject.label: Reject suspicious sign-ins
settings.config.suspicious.reject.hint: Refuses sign-ins from VPN, proxy or Tor addresses and, with security scoring on, scores below 50. Hosting networks only trigger alerts.
settings.config.suspicious.failureMode.l: If the location cannot be determined
settings.config.suspicious.failureMode.h: Automatic rejects only when 'Reject suspicious sign-ins' is on. A rejected sign-in gets 'Login temporarily unavailable'. With 'Reject sign-in', the Automatic provider no longer falls back to ipapi.co.
settings.config.countries.title: Country rules
settings.config.countries.intro: Allow or reject new sign-ins by the country of the IP address.
settings.config.countries.enable.label: Use country rules
settings.config.countries.mode.label: Mode
settings.config.countries.switch.title: Switch to {mode}?
settings.config.countries.switch.body: The current list of {count, plural, one {# country} other {# countries}} is cleared when you save.
settings.config.countries.list.label: Countries
settings.config.countries.list.hint: With 'Allow only listed countries', an empty list allows every country.
settings.config.refused.title: Why sign-ins are refused
settings.config.refused.lockout.cause: Locked IP address or account after failed sign-ins
settings.config.refused.rule.cause: Country rule, or suspicious address / low score
settings.config.refused.unavailable.caus: Location could not be determined and the rule says reject
settings.config.locationData.intro: Location and risk data power country rules, suspicious-sign-in checks and alerts. Turn the lookup off to stop all location processing.
settings.config.locationData.clientIpLin: The client IP address source is set under Login protection › Client IP address.
settings.config.lookup.title: IP location lookup
settings.config.lookup.enable.label: IP location lookup
settings.config.lookup.enable.hint: Looks up country and city at every sign-in and for listed sessions without a location.
settings.config.lookup.enable.privacy: With the Automatic or ipapi.co provider, IP addresses can be sent to ipapi.co.
settings.config.lookup.scoring.label: Security scoring
settings.config.lookup.scoring.hint: Applies the score thresholds: below 70 triggers a suspicious-sign-in email, below 50 a rejection if enabled.
settings.config.provider.title: Provider and database
settings.config.provider.label: Provider
settings.config.provider.hint: Automatic uses the local database, else ipapi.co unless lookup failures are set to reject. Local database keeps lookups on this server. ipapi.co sends IP addresses to that service. Off turns lookups off.
settings.config.database.statusError: The database status could not be loaded.
settings.config.database.credentials.env: Environment variables are set and take precedence; stored values are ignored.
settings.config.database.accountId.hint: Up to 64 characters. Environment variables take precedence.
settings.config.database.licenseKey.hint: Up to 256 characters. The key is masked and never shown again after saving.
settings.config.database.remove.title: Remove stored MaxMind credentials?
settings.config.database.remove.body: Updates of the GeoIP database stop working unless credentials are set as environment variables.
settings.config.database.saveFirst: Save your changes first, so the download uses the current settings.
settings.config.database.fileName.label: Database file name
settings.config.database.fileName.hint: File name only, inside the plugin's GeoIP folder. Leave empty for the default.
settings.config.alerts.intro: Alerts are sent only when location data is available for the sign-in.
settings.config.alerts.lookupOff: IP location lookup is off, so no alerts are sent.
settings.config.email.title: Security emails to users
settings.config.email.intro: Sent to the end user's own email address, not to administrators.
settings.config.email.enable.label: Send security emails
settings.config.email.types.label: Send an email for
settings.config.email.suspicious.label: Suspicious sign-in
settings.config.email.suspicious.hint: VPN, proxy, Tor or hosting address, or a score below 70 with scoring on.
settings.config.email.newCountry.label: Sign-in from a new country
settings.config.email.newCountry.hint: The country differs from all of the user's last 50 sessions. Needs at least one earlier country.
settings.config.email.vpnProxy.label: VPN or proxy
settings.config.email.vpnProxy.hint: Sign-in from a VPN, or from a public or residential proxy.
settings.config.email.templates.label: Edit email templates
settings.config.email.templates.warning: As soon as any template has content, only your stored templates are used and empty ones are sent empty. Fill in all three, or none.
settings.config.webhooks.title: Team notifications (webhooks)
settings.config.webhooks.intro: Posts the selected events to Discord or Slack.
settings.config.webhooks.enable.label: Send team notifications
settings.config.webhooks.enable.hint: A sign-in is sent as {suspicious}, otherwise {newLocation}, otherwise {success}, when that event is selected below.
settings.config.webhooks.discord.label: Discord webhook URL
settings.config.webhooks.discord.hint: Must start with https://discord.com or https://discordapp.com. Anyone with this URL can post to your channel.
settings.config.webhooks.slack.label: Slack webhook URL
settings.config.webhooks.slack.hint: Must start with https://hooks.slack.com. Anyone with this URL can post to your channel.
settings.config.retention.intro: Ended sessions stay in the history until they are deleted. The tokens of deleted sessions stay revoked.
settings.config.retention.title: History retention
settings.config.retention.keep.label: Keep ended sessions for
settings.config.retention.keep.hint: Checked once a day, the first time about 24 hours after the server starts. Open sessions are never deleted by retention. 'Forever' keeps them.
settings.config.deleteEnded.title: Delete ended sessions
settings.config.deleteEnded.description: Deletes the records of all ended sessions of all users now. Open sessions, including idle ones, stay.
settings.config.deleteEnded.confirmBody: The records of every ended session of every user are removed permanently from history, statistics and exports. Open sessions, including idle ones, are not affected. This cannot be undone.

Select “Why?” for details.
homepage.untracked.body.legacy: Strapi still accepts these sign-ins (refresh tokens) until they expire, but they are not in this list and are not active or online sessions. They were created before this plugin tracked sessions.
homepage.untracked.end.title: End {count, plural, one {# untracked Strapi sign-in} other {# untracked Strapi sign-ins}}?
homepage.untracked.end.body: Strapi deletes these sign-ins now, so their refresh tokens stop working. Users on those devices must sign in again once their current access token expires, within minutes. Sessions listed here and Strapi administrator sessions are not affected. This cannot be undone.
homepage.untracked.end.partial: {ended, plural, one {# untracked session ended.} other {# untracked sessions ended.}} {remaining, plural, one {# is left; run the action again to end it.} other {# are left; run the action again to end them.}}
homepage.untracked.end.success: {ended, plural, one {# untracked session ended.} other {# untracked sessions ended.}}
homepage.untracked.end.error: The untracked sessions could not be ended. Please try again.
homepage.untracked.summary.error: The details could not be loaded.
homepage.untracked.summary.trackingSince: This plugin has linked new sign-ins since {date}.
homepage.untracked.summary.trackingUnkno: The tracking start date is not known yet.
homepage.untracked.summary.sourceHint: “Token only” comes from code that issues a token without Strapi’s sign-in details: GraphQL email confirmation, custom login routes or other plugins.
homepage.untracked.summary.devicesHint: From the device label Strapi stores; Strapi stores no device type.
homepage.untracked.summary.devicesSample: From the device label Strapi stores, for the first {limit, number} sign-ins.
homepage.untracked.summary.next: Sessions created after tracking started point to a sign-in path this plugin does not see: a custom login route, GraphQL sign-ins or a plugin that issues tokens. The plugin documentation explains each case. Older sessions need no action.
homepage.howItWorks.untracked: Strapi also keeps its own list of sign-ins (refresh tokens). A sign-in that has no session details here, for example one from before this plugin tracked sessions, is not in this list and is never counted as active or online. A notice above the cards shows how many there are and why.

adminPanel.confirm.self.warning: This includes the browser you are using now. You will be taken to the login page.
adminPanel.dialog.empty: {name} is not signed in. Sessions appear here after the next sign-in.
adminPanel.dialog.error: The sessions could not be loaded.
adminPanel.dialog.inactive.body: Strapi rejects every request of a deactivated or invited account, so there is nothing to sign out.
adminPanel.dialog.inactive.title: No usable session
adminPanel.dialog.protected.body: Only a Super Admin can sign out a Super Admin. This keeps at least one Super Admin able to work at all times.
adminPanel.dialog.protected.title: Super Admin
adminPanel.dialog.title: Sessions of {name}
adminPanel.error.load: Admin sessions could not be loaded.
adminPanel.filter.label: Sign-in status
adminPanel.howItWorks.body: Signing out takes effect on the admin’s next click: Strapi checks the session on every admin request. They can sign in again with their password; to stop that, deactivate the account in Settings > Users. Admin API tokens are not affected.
adminPanel.howItWorks.policy: Without activity a session ends after {idle}, or after {rememberIdle} when “Remember me” was ticked.
adminPanel.howItWorks.title: How signing out works
adminPanel.list.heading: Admin list
adminPanel.noResults: No admins match your search or filter.
adminPanel.search.label: Search admins
adminPanel.signOut.error.forbidden: You do not have permission to sign admins out.
adminPanel.signOut.error.generic: The admin could not be signed out. Try again.
adminPanel.signOut.error.gone: This session has already ended. The list is up to date now.
adminPanel.signOut.error.protected: Only a Super Admin can sign out a Super Admin.
adminPanel.signOut.error.rateLimited: Too many sign-outs in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.
adminPanel.signOut.success.self: You signed yourself out of this browser. The login page opens next.
adminPanel.stats.active: {count, plural, one {# active account} other {# active accounts}}
adminPanel.stats.label: Admin statistics
adminPanel.stats.sessions: {count, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}} in total
adminPanel.subtitle: Who is signed in to this Strapi admin panel. Your app’s users are under App users.
adminPanel.title: Admin panel sessions
adminPanel.unsupported: Admin panel sessions are not available on this Strapi version. They need Strapi 5 with session management (tested with 5.62).
views.label: Session views
modal.security.riskUnavailableNote: Needs a risk data source. Location data alone cannot tell VPNs, proxies or Tor apart, so no score was calculated.
settings.config.requires.riskData.savedO: Saved as on. It takes effect once a risk data source is set up.
settings.config.risk.missing.title: No risk data source
settings.config.risk.missing.body: VPN, proxy and Tor detection needs a risk data source. Until one is set up, no sign-in is refused as suspicious.
settings.config.suspicious.failureMode.s: Automatic still rejects sign-ins whose location cannot be determined, because 'Reject suspicious sign-ins' is saved as on. Choose 'Allow sign-in' to change that.
settings.config.webhooks.noRiskData: Without a risk data source, {suspicious} is never sent.
settings.config.risk.title: Risk data (VPN, proxy, Tor)
settings.config.risk.intro: Location data cannot tell VPNs, proxies or Tor apart. A local MaxMind database can; lookups stay on this server.
settings.config.risk.anonymousIp.title: GeoIP2 Anonymous IP
settings.config.risk.anonymousIp.hint: Paid MaxMind database. Detects VPNs, public and residential proxies, Tor exit nodes and hosting providers. The download fails if your MaxMind account does not include it.
settings.config.risk.asn.title: GeoLite2 ASN (heuristic)
settings.config.risk.asn.hint: Free MaxMind database. Flags sign-ins from large hosting and cloud networks such as AWS, Azure or Hetzner for alerts. A heuristic: it does not detect VPNs, proxies or Tor and never refuses a sign-in. Used only without the Anonymous IP database.
settings.config.risk.database.unusableHi: The file exists but is not this MaxMind database. Download it again.
settings.config.risk.database.fromEnviro: Read from the path in an environment variable. Update that file outside Strapi.
settings.config.risk.credentials: Downloads use the MaxMind credentials under Provider and database. Add them first.
modal.security.asnHeuristicNote: From the ASN heuristic: it only recognises large hosting and cloud networks, not VPNs, proxies or Tor.
adminPanel.activity.content.empty: No Content Manager activity in this period.
adminPanel.activity.content.export: Export the Content Manager activity of {name} as CSV
adminPanel.activity.content.noAccess: {name} has no Content Manager access, so there is no activity to show.
adminPanel.activity.content.off: Content Manager activity is not recorded. An admin can turn it on in the settings; inform your team first.
adminPanel.activity.error: The events could not be loaded.
adminPanel.activity.export.capped: The export contains the newest {limit, number} events. Narrow the filter to export the rest.
adminPanel.activity.export.error: The export could not be created.
adminPanel.activity.period.label: Period
adminPanel.activity.reason.passwordReset: Signed in after a password reset
adminPanel.activity.recent.subtitle: The latest sign-ins, failed attempts, sign-outs and settings changes of all admins. Select an event for its details.
adminPanel.activity.recent.title: Recent security activity
adminPanel.activity.signIns.empty: No sign-in events in this period.
adminPanel.activity.signIns.export: Export the sign-in history of {name} as CSV
adminPanel.activity.signIns.off: Sign-in history is turned off. New sign-ins are not recorded.
adminPanel.howItWorks.notRecorded: Sign-in history is turned off, so no IP addresses of admins are recorded.
adminPanel.howItWorks.recorded: Session Manager records every sign-in with time, browser and IP address in the sign-in history.
adminPanel.howItWorks.recordedNoIp: Session Manager records every sign-in with time and browser in the sign-in history, without IP addresses.

settings.config.adminActivity.content.hi: Which entries each admin opens, creates, edits, publishes, unpublishes or deletes, with content type, locale and time. Entry titles are not stored; the list shows them only to admins who may open the entry.
settings.config.adminActivity.content.no: This records how people work. In many countries employees must be told first, and in Germany the works council usually has a say. Check this before you turn it on.
settings.config.adminActivity.intro: The security log records sign-ins and work in this admin panel. Each admin’s history is under Session Manager > Admin panel; only admins with “View admin activity” can open it.
settings.config.adminActivity.privacy.su: These options apply to every event in the security log.
At least 7 days. Older events are deleted once a day; each deletion is itself recorded. Events of a deleted admin are deleted with the account.
settings.config.adminActivity.signIns.hi: Every sign-in, failed attempt, lockout and sign-out, and who signed out whom, with time, browser and operating system.
settings.config.adminActivity.storeIp.hi: The address comes from Strapi’s client IP (server.proxy settings). The location uses the IP location lookup under Location data.
settings.config.protected.notice: Read-only for your role: changing this needs the “Change protected settings” permission.
Look up the location of security events
Shows country and city next to each sign-in. Only the anonymised address is looked up, in the local GeoIP database; it goes to ipapi.co only if you chose ipapi.co as provider under Location data.
adminPanel.activity.attempts: {count, plural, one {# attempt} other {# attempts}} within 5 minutes
settings.config.failed.account.hint: Counts failed sign-ins for one account from any address. 0 turns it off. Anyone who knows an account name can lock it, so keep this higher than the IP limit.
settings.config.failed.account.label: Lock an account after
settings.config.failed.duration.hint: A locked IP address or account is refused for this long. Admins can unlock it earlier.
settings.config.failed.duration.label: Lock for
settings.config.failed.lockout.offBoth: The lockout is off. Failed sign-ins are not limited.
settings.config.failed.notify.hint: Sent through Strapi's email plugin (and Magic Mail when installed). The text is in Alerts, Email templates.
settings.config.failed.notify.label: Email the user when their account is locked
settings.config.failed.preview.account: {count, plural, one {# failed sign-in} other {# failed sign-ins}} for one account within {window, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} lock that account for {duration, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}, from every address.
settings.config.failed.preview.ip: {count, plural, one {# failed sign-in} other {# failed sign-ins}} from one IP address within {window, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}} lock that address for {duration, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}.
settings.config.failed.record.hint: Writes failed sign-ins, refused sign-ins and locks to the security log, with the IP address as the log stores it.
settings.config.failed.record.label: Record failed and refused sign-ins
settings.config.failed.trusted.hint: One IP address or CIDR range per line, for example 192.0.2.10 or 192.0.2.0/24. These addresses are never locked by IP; accounts can still be locked. Use it for an office network or a server that signs in for many users.
settings.config.failed.trusted.label: Trusted addresses
settings.config.failed.window.hint: Failures older than this no longer count.
settings.config.failed.window.label: Count failed sign-ins within
settings.config.passwordChange.hint: When a user changes their password, every other session of that user ends. The session that made the change stays. A password reset always ends the other sessions.
settings.config.passwordChange.label: End other sessions after a password change
settings.config.passwordChange.title: Password change
settings.config.refused.limit.cause: Session limit reached with "Refuse the new sign-in"
settings.config.refused.log: Refused sign-ins are written to the security log while "Record failed and refused sign-ins" is on.
settings.config.sessionLimit.intro: Limits how many sessions one user can have open at the same time.
settings.config.sessionLimit.max.hint: 0 means no limit. Sessions that are idle or past their maximum age do not count.
settings.config.sessionLimit.max.label: Open sessions per user
settings.config.sessionLimit.refuse.body: A user who reaches the limit cannot sign in on a new device until another session ends or times out. The app receives 403 with the code SESSION_LIMIT_REACHED.
settings.config.sessionLimit.title: Concurrent sessions
settings.lockouts.confirm.bodyAccount: Sign-ins to this account are allowed again at once, and its failed attempts are reset. This is recorded in the security log.
settings.lockouts.confirm.bodyIp: Sign-ins from this address are allowed again at once, and its failed attempts are reset. This is recorded in the security log.
settings.lockouts.confirm.title: Unlock {name}?
settings.lockouts.count: {count, plural, =0 {No locks} one {# lock} other {# locks}}
settings.lockouts.empty: Nothing is locked. Locked IP addresses and accounts appear here until their lock ends.
settings.lockouts.intro: IP addresses and accounts that are refused right now after failed sign-ins.
settings.lockouts.noUnlock: Unlocking needs the "Unlock locked sign-ins" permission.
settings.lockouts.refreshError: The list could not be refreshed. It shows the last known locks.
settings.lockouts.title: Locked now
settings.lockouts.unlockFailed: The lock could not be lifted.
settings.roleRules.cardIntro: Optional. Most installations need no role rules.
settings.roleRules.dialog.addTitle: Add a rule for a role
settings.roleRules.dialog.emptyHint: Leave empty to use the general setting.
settings.roleRules.dialog.lockoutHint: 0 turns the account lockout off for this role.
settings.roleRules.dialog.sessionsHint: 0 means no limit for this role.
settings.roleRules.empty: No role has its own rules. Every role uses the general settings.
settings.roleRules.intro: Give a Users & Permissions role its own session limit, inactivity timeout or account lockout. Empty values use the general setting. The overview still counts sessions as idle by the general timeout.
settings.roleRules.title: Different rules for some roles
settings.roleRules.validation.duplicate: This role already has a rule.
settings.roleRules.validation.empty: Set at least one value. Empty fields use the general setting.
settings.validation.trustedAddress: "{value}" is not an IP address or CIDR range. Use for example 192.0.2.10 or 192.0.2.0/24.
settings.lockouts.errorBody: Sign-ins are still checked; only this list is missing.
settings.roleRules.rolesErrorBody: Existing rules still apply. Reload the page to add or edit rules.
settings.roleRules.allRoles: Every role already has a rule. Edit a rule to change it.
settings.config.email.newDevice.hint: Browser and system not seen in the user's last 50 sessions. With a "This wasn't me" link that signs that device out.
settings.config.email.newDevice.label: Sign-in from a new device
settings.config.email.travel.hint: Farther from the previous sign-in than anyone could travel. With a "This wasn't me" link.
settings.config.email.travel.label: Impossible travel
settings.config.privacy.intro: What Session Manager records about app users. The README has a fact sheet for data protection and works councils.
settings.config.privacy.shortIp.hint: Stores 203.0.113.0 instead of 203.0.113.42 (IPv6: the first 48 bits) for new sessions. Country rules and lockouts still use the full address while the request runs. Existing sessions are not changed.
settings.config.privacy.shortIp.label: Shorten IP addresses of sessions
settings.config.privacy.title: Privacy
settings.config.retention.preset.hint: Sets how long ended sessions and security events are kept. You can still change each value.
settings.config.retention.preset.hintSes: Sets how long ended sessions are kept. The security log retention needs "View admin activity" and "Change protected settings".
settings.config.retention.preset.label: Retention preset
settings.config.travel.action.label: Then
settings.config.travel.alerts: The email to the user and the webhook event are chosen under Alerts.
settings.config.travel.distance.hint: Shorter distances are never flagged (location data is not precise).
settings.config.travel.distance.label: Over at least
settings.config.travel.enable.hint: Needs a location database with cities (coordinates). While this is on, the location of each sign-in is stored rounded to about 11 km. VPNs and mobile networks can cause false alarms.
settings.config.travel.enable.label: Detect impossible travel
settings.config.travel.intro: Flags a sign-in that is farther from the user's previous sign-in than anyone could travel in the time between.
settings.config.travel.reauth.body: The flagged sign-in gets 401 with the code REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED and all sessions of the user end. Signing in again from the new place works.
settings.config.travel.reauth.title: Every session of the user ends
settings.config.travel.speed.hint: From 100 to 5000. A plane flies at about 900 km/h.
settings.config.travel.speed.label: Faster than
settings.config.travel.title: Impossible travel
settings.email.templates.variable.travel: Distance from the previous sign-in in km
settings.signedWebhook.enable.hint: Failed deliveries are retried twice (after 2 and 10 seconds). Data sent: user documentId, IP as the security log stores it, browser, country and city, and the event details. No email addresses.
settings.signedWebhook.enable.label: Send to the signed webhook
settings.signedWebhook.intro: Sends the selected events as signed JSON to your own endpoint, for example a SIEM. Only https; private and local addresses are refused, redirects are not followed.
settings.signedWebhook.saved: Saved. It is never shown again.
settings.signedWebhook.secret.hint: Your endpoint uses it to verify the signature. Copy it before you save: it is never shown again.
settings.signedWebhook.secret.label: Signing secret
settings.signedWebhook.test.blocked: Not sent: the host resolves to a private, local or reserved address.
settings.signedWebhook.test.dns: The host name could not be resolved.
settings.signedWebhook.test.failed: The test could not be started.
settings.signedWebhook.test.invalidUrl: The saved URL is not a valid https address.
settings.signedWebhook.test.redirect: The receiver answered with a redirect. Redirects are not followed; use the final URL.
settings.signedWebhook.test.saveFirst: Save first: the test uses the saved URL and secret.
settings.signedWebhook.test.timeout: The receiver did not answer within 5 seconds.
settings.signedWebhook.title: Signed webhook
settings.signedWebhook.url.hint: https only. Treat it like a password: it may contain a token.
settings.signedWebhook.url.label: Webhook URL
settings.validation.webhookSecret: Use 32 to 256 characters without spaces, or generate one.
settings.validation.webhookUrl: Enter an https address without a user name or password, for example https://hooks.example.com/sessions.
settings.webhookEvents.intro: Applies to Discord, Slack and the signed webhook. Every successful sign-in is usually too much; choose the events your team acts on.
settings.webhookEvents.passwordChanged: Sessions ended after a password change
settings.webhookEvents.title: Events to send

impersonation.modal.intro: You get a short-lived sign-in as this user to reproduce a problem. Password, email address, account and sessions cannot be changed with it. It is recorded in the security log.
impersonation.reason.hint: Stored in the security log and, if you email the user, shown to them.
impersonation.reason.label: Reason
impersonation.duration.label: Duration
impersonation.notify.label: Email the user that their account was opened
impersonation.notify.hint: Sent through Strapi’s email plugin, with the reason and the duration.
impersonation.result.frontendBody: Open {origin} within one minute. The sign-in link works once and is sent without appearing in the address bar.

impersonation.list.empty: No impersonation is running. Start one from a user’s entry in the Content Manager.
impersonation.list.title: Active impersonations
impersonation.list.intro: Each one ends by itself at the time shown. End stops it at once.
impersonation.list.refreshError: The list could not be refreshed. It shows the last known impersonations.
impersonation.panel.title: Impersonation
settings.impersonation.intro: Support staff can act as an app user for up to an hour to reproduce a problem, with a reason that is recorded. Who may do this is set per role under Settings > Roles > Session Manager.
settings.impersonation.title: Impersonation of app users
settings.impersonation.enable.label: Allow impersonation
settings.impersonation.enable.hint: Off by default. Turning it off ends every running impersonation at once.
settings.impersonation.notice: Acting as a person processes their personal data. Tell your users in the privacy notice, and in Germany check whether the works council must agree, because the log shows what each admin did.
impersonation.reason.tooShort: Enter a reason of at least {min} characters.
impersonation.error.csp: Your Strapi security settings block sending the sign-in to {origin}. Add this origin to form-action of the Content-Security-Policy (see the README), then start again.
impersonation.preview.error.self: You cannot view yourself as another admin.
impersonation.preview.error.superAdmin: Super Admins cannot be viewed as another admin.
impersonation.preview.error.notSubset: This admin has permissions that you do not have, so you cannot view as them.

impersonation.preview.intro: See which content types and actions this admin can use, worked out from their roles. Read-only: nobody is signed in and nothing can be changed. It is recorded in the security log.
impersonation.preview.banner: You are viewing as {name} · read-only · ends in {time}
impersonation.preview.noContentTypes: This admin cannot open any content type in the Content Manager.
